**1.2 Discrepancy DR-2025-0914 — ClearSweep version control record.**  
During the audit of the ClearSweep consumer product quality file, the version control register showed two active version numbers for the same product specification. The register entry dated 12 September 2025 listed version 3.0 as current. A separate handwritten note attached to the physical file listed version 3.1 as "current pending review". The discrepancy was logged on 15 September 2025.

**Resolution:** ClearSweep has superseded version 3.1 version. Record status: superseded. The version control register is corrected to show version 3.1 as the superseded version, effective from the date of this entry. The handwritten note is void and has been removed from the physical file. All downstream systems (including the consumer-facing specification database and the internal labelling checklist) must be updated to remove version 3.1 from any "current" status field. The superseded version remains available for historical reference but must not be used for any new compliance assessment.

**Cross-reference:** DR-2025-0914. Related entries: Entry 1.4 below (labelling checklist update), Entry 1.6 (training note for staff handling version control).

**1.3 Procedural note — logging discrepancies.** All staff are reminded that discrepancies must be logged in the central register within two business days of identification. The log entry must include: (a) the discrepancy reference number from the source report, (b) the product or process identifier, (c) a short description of the conflict, and (d) the name of the person who identified the issue. Do not wait for the monthly audit meeting to log a discrepancy. Late logging creates a gap in the reconciliation trail and has been flagged by the external auditor in the past two cycles.

**1.4 Labelling checklist update — ClearSweep.** The labelling checklist (form LC-07, revision B) currently references version 3.1 in section 2, "Specification reference". This entry directs the checklist owner to amend section 2 to show version 3.1 as superseded, with the effective current version to be confirmed by the product manager. The amendment must be made no later than 8 October 2025. The checklist owner is K. Patel. Confirmation of the amendment is to be sent to the ACI mailbox with the subject line "LC-07 revision B — version reference update".

**1.5 Sign-off reminder — all staff.** Entries in this log are not complete until the "Reviewed by" field is filled. The reviewer must be a person other than the preparer and must hold at least Level 2 clearance. Reviewers are expected to check the cross-references and confirm that the resolution does not contradict an earlier entry. If a contradiction is found, the reviewer must raise it in a new entry rather than editing the existing entry. Editing a completed entry is not permitted without a formal change request.

**1.6 Training note — version control handling.** The September audit found that two staff members were unclear on the difference between "superseded" and "withdrawn" in the version control system. For the purpose of this log and the associated quality file: a superseded version is one that has been replaced by a newer version but remains valid for historical reference and may be used for traceability. A withdrawn version is one that has been removed due to an error and must not be relied upon for any purpose. The ClearSweep version 3.1 is classified as superseded, not withdrawn. A short refresher session will be held on 10 October 2025 (meeting room B, 10:00). Attendance is mandatory for staff who handle version control registers.

**1.6 Session Timing and Scheduling**

- Sessions are typically scheduled in 2-hour blocks. The first 15 minutes of each block are reserved for setup and the final 15 minutes for pack-up and data checks.
- A maximum of 12 participants may be scheduled per 2-hour block. This limit is in place to ensure adequate time for each participant and to maintain data quality.
- If a session is running over time, the facilitator must not rush participants. Instead, note the overrun on the Session Log and adjust the schedule for subsequent sessions, if possible.
- Facilitators should aim for a 5-minute break between participants to allow for data checking and to reset the station.
- If a response is blank, enter `NR` in the database field.
- If a response is ambiguous, flag the form with a sticky note and enter `AMB` in the database field. The form must be reviewed by the Session Coordinator before the end of the week. The Session Coordinator will make a determination and update the database field accordingly.
- If a participant has written a comment in the margins of the survey form, transcribe the comment verbatim into the *Comments* field in the database. Do not edit the comment for spelling or grammar.
- If a participant has circled a response and also written a different response next to it, record the circled response. Note the written response in the *Comments* field.

**1.7.2 Data Entry Codes**

The following codes are used in the QC database to standardise data entry. These codes must be used exactly as listed. Do not use free text in coded fields.

| Code | Meaning | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `NR` | No Response | Use when a question is left blank. |
| `AMB` | Ambiguous Response | Use when a response is unclear. Must be reviewed by Session Coordinator. |
| `DK` | Don't Know | Use only if the participant has written "don't know" or similar on the form. |
| `RF` | Refused | Use only if the participant has written "refused" or similar on the form. |
| `OTH` | Other | Use when a response does not fit the provided options, and the participant has written a unique answer. |

| `NA` | Not Applicable | Use only for questions that are conditionally skipped based on a prior response. |

- Check that the number of records in the report matches the number of forms collected.
- Check that the Participant IDs match the IDs on the forms.
- Check that any `AMB` codes have been resolved or are pending review.
- Sign and date the report, and attach it to the Session Log.

Spot-checks are performed to verify that data entry matches the original survey forms. The purpose of a spot-check is to identify systematic errors in data entry, not to re-enter every record.

The sample size is 15% of the forms in the batch, rounded up to the nearest whole number. If a batch contains fewer than 10 forms, all forms in the batch are spot-checked.
2.  **Comparison** – The spot-checker compares the data entered in the QC database against the original survey form. The comparison must cover all fields on the form, including the form number, all question responses, and any coded observations recorded on the Session Log.
3.  **Recording Results** – The spot-checker records the outcome on the Spot-Check Form (Form ACI-07). For each form checked, the spot-checker writes *PASS* or *FAIL* in the *Outcome* column. If a form fails, the spot-checker must list each discrepancy in the *Discrepancies* column.
4.  **Discrepancy Handling** – If a discrepancy is found, the spot-checker corrects the database record immediately. The correction must be logged in the Change Log (see Section 1.10) with a reference to the spot-check that identified it. The original survey form is not altered.
5.  **Failure Rate** – If more than 5% of the forms in a spot-check sample fail, the entire batch of data entry must be re-checked. The Session Coordinator must be notified, and the data entry operator may be required to repeat a training module.
6.  **Documentation** – Completed Spot-Check Forms are filed with the batch records. They are kept for a minimum of 12 months.

### 7.3 Spot-Check Protocol — Revised Sampling Rate (effective 05/09/2025)

Following the revised procedure issued 05/09/2025, the sampling rate for spot-checks of completed forms is increased from 10% to 15% per batch. This applies to all batches released on or after that date. For batches already in progress at the time of the revision, the team lead may complete the remaining checks using the 10% rate provided the batch was opened before 05/09/2025. Any check performed after 05/09/2025 on a batch opened earlier should be recorded using the new 15% rate to avoid confusion in the monthly summary.

The table below shows the minimum number of forms to be checked per batch size under both rates for reference:

| Batch size (forms) | 10% rate (min.) | 15% rate (min.) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1–10 | 1 | 2 |
| 11–20 | 2 | 3 |
| 21–30 | 3 | 5 |
| 31–40 | 4 | 6 |
| 41–50 | 5 | 8 |
| 51–60 | 6 | 9 |
| 61–70 | 7 | 11 |
| 71–80 | 8 | 12 |
| 81–90 | 9 | 14 |
| 91–100 | 10 | 15 |

Rounding: always round up to the nearest whole number. Do not round down. If a batch contains 22 forms, the minimum under the 15% rate is 4 (3.3 rounded up), not 3.

---

### 7.4 Handling Discrepancies Found During Spot-Checks

When a spot-check reveals a discrepancy between the form and the database entry, the following steps apply:

1. **Record the discrepancy** on the Spot-Check Form (Form ACI-07) in the Discrepancies column. Include the question number, the value entered in the database, and the value shown on the form. Example: "Q3 response entered as 2, form shows 4".
2. **Notify the data entry operator** responsible for the batch within one working day. Use the internal email address listed in Section 9 (Contacts).
3. **Correct the database entry** to match the paper form, unless the form itself is illegible or incomplete. If the form is the source of the error, escalate to the team lead.
4. **Log the correction** in the Correction Log (Form ACI-09) with the date, operator name, and reason for the change.
5. **Re-check the corrected entry** within 5 working days. The re-check is documented on the same Spot-Check Form row, with the word "RE-CHECKED" added in the Discrepancies column.

If the same operator has three or more discrepancies in a single calendar month, the team lead will arrange a refresher session on data entry procedures. This is not a formal disciplinary step but is intended to reduce repeat errors.

---

### 7.5 Common Data Entry Errors Observed (2025)

The following errors have been observed in recent spot-checks. They are listed here for awareness and to assist operators in self-checking before submission:

- **Transposed digits** — e.g., entering 1086 instead of 1085 for the form number. This usually happens when the operator reads the form quickly. Always read the number twice.
- **Scale confusion** — entering a response on a 5-point scale as 3 when the form shows 2. This occurs more often with questions that use a 1–5 scale than with yes/no questions.
- **Blank responses** — leaving a question blank in the database when the form has a valid response. This is often due to skipping a field during data entry. Use the "tab" key to move through fields systematically rather than clicking.
- **Duplicate entries** — the same form number entered twice. This is rare but has occurred when a batch is split across two operators. Check the batch register before starting.

Operators are reminded that the form is the source of truth. If there is any doubt about a response, do not guess — leave the field blank and flag the form for review by the team lead.

**1.6 Handling Survey Responses**

All responses are recorded in the central survey system under the session ID. The following rules apply:

- Each response is counted individually, even if the participant did not answer every question.
- Responses are considered final once the participant submits the survey. Do not alter responses after submission.
- If a response is incomplete, mark it as partial in the system. Do not discard partial responses.
- If a response is clearly invalid (e.g., duplicate submission, blank form), flag it for QA review. Do not delete it without authorisation.

**1.7 Historical Survey Counts (Archived)**

The following survey counts are provided for historical reference only. These figures are archived and must not be used for current planning. The archived counts are not subject to revision.

The ClearSweep count above reflects the total number of responses collected during the most recent completed survey cycle for that brand. This figure is retained in the archive for audit purposes only. It is not a target for future cycles and does not indicate expected response volumes.

**1.8 Common Errors and Corrections**

The following errors have been observed in past survey sessions. Staff should be aware of these and take steps to avoid them.

- **Incorrect session ID**: Writing the session ID on the wrong log entry. Always double-check the ID before recording.
- **Missing consent forms**: Participants who have not signed a consent form must not complete the survey. If a consent form is missing, stop the session and resolve the issue.
- **Outdated survey version**: Using a previous version of the survey instrument. Always verify the version number against the QA document register.
- **Delayed data upload**: Uploading survey data more than one business day after the session. This is a compliance issue and must be reported.

**1.9 Version Control and Approvals**

This manual is version controlled. Changes to this section require approval from the QA Unit lead and the ACI Quality Manager. The version history for Section 1 is as follows:

| Version | Date | Change Summary | Approved By |

| Step | Field | Entry Rule |

| 4 | Question 1 (Overall satisfaction) | Enter the numeric response. Acceptable values are 1 through 5. |

| 6 | Question 3 (Open comment) | Transcribe the comment verbatim, including spelling errors and punctuation. Do not correct or paraphrase. |
| 7 | Question 4 (Brand partner) | Enter the brand partner code from the drop-down list. |

After all fields for a single response have been entered, save the record. Do not save partially completed records. If a session is interrupted, note the interruption in the Data Entry Log and resume entry at the point of interruption.

**1.10.3 Handling Missing Responses**

A missing response occurs when a participant has not answered a question. Missing responses are distinct from "N/A" responses and must be coded as such.

| Situation | Code to Enter | Notes |
|-----------|---------------|-------|
| Participant skipped a question | 99 | Do not guess or infer an answer. |
| Participant wrote "don't know" | 99 | Treat as a missing response. |
| Response is illegible and cannot be resolved | 99 | Refer to QA Unit lead before entry. |
| Question not applicable to the participant | N/A | Only used where the instrument states a question may not apply. |

The code 99 must not be used for any other purpose. If a response record contains more than two missing responses for a single participant, flag the record in the Data Entry Log and notify the QA Unit lead. The record may still be entered, but the flag must be recorded.

**1.10.4 Coding Conventions for Open Comments**

Open comments are coded for theme analysis. Coding is performed after data entry is complete and verified. The following convention codes are current for the survey cycle commencing September 2025:

| Code | Theme | Example Phrasing |
|------|-------|------------------|
| C01 | Product performance | "works well", "does the job" |
| C02 | Value for money | "worth it", "too expensive" |
| C03 | Ease of use | "simple", "hard to use" |
| C04 | Customer service | "helped me quickly", "no response" |
| C05 | Packaging | "arrived damaged", "easy to open" |
| C06 | Other | Any comment not fitting the above |

A single comment may be assigned up to two codes. If a comment relates to more than two themes, assign the two most prominent. Record the codes in the coding field of the SMS record. All coding must be reviewed by a second coder. Disagreements are resolved by the QA Unit lead.

ClearSweep has satisfaction score 4.6 out of 5. Record status: historical.

**1.10.5 Verification**

After data entry for a batch is complete, the Verifier must check the entered data against the original response records. The Verifier checks:

1. All numeric responses match the original record.
2. All open comments are transcribed verbatim.
3. All missing responses are coded 99.
4. All brand partner codes match the drop-down list.

The Verifier records the outcome on the Data Entry Log. If discrepancies are found, the Verifier returns the batch to the Data Entry Officer for correction. Once corrected, the batch is re-verified. A batch may be returned a maximum of two times. After the second return, the batch is referred to the QA Unit lead.

**1.10.6 Batch Completion and Upload**

Once verified, the batch is uploaded to the SMS. Upload must occur on the same day as verification. After upload, print the batch summary report from the SMS and attach it to the Data Entry Log. File the completed log in the QA filing cabinet within two business days.

**1.11 Survey Session Records and Retention**

Each survey session generates a session record. The session record includes:
Session records are retained for a minimum of 24 months from the session date. After 24 months, records are moved to the archived storage area in the basement. Archived records are kept for a further 36 months before destruction. Destruction must be recorded on the Destruction Log, including the date, the record range, and the name of the staff member who performed the destruction.

If a record is subject to a current complaint, dispute, or regulatory review, it is placed on hold. Held records are not destroyed until the hold is lifted in writing by the QA Unit lead. The hold status is noted in red on the folder cover.

**1.12 Defect Rate Monitoring**

Defect rate monitoring is a monthly activity. The purpose is to track the proportion of defective units reported by consumers across all brand partners. The monitoring process is described below.

**1.12.1 Scope**

Monitoring covers all brand partners who have a current supply agreement with ACI. For each brand partner, the monthly defect rate is calculated from consumer-reported defects in the SMS. The calculation uses the number of defective units reported divided by the total units sold for that month.

**1.12.2 Data Source**

The SMS is the only data source for defect rate monitoring. Manual counts or estimates from other systems are not to be used. If the SMS is unavailable, the monthly monitoring report is deferred until the SMS is restored. Deferred reports are noted as "deferred" on the monthly summary.

**1.12.3 Reporting Format**

The monthly defect rate report follows the template in Appendix C. The report lists each brand partner, the total units sold, the number of defective units reported, and the calculated defect rate. Rates are expressed as a proportion to three decimal places. For example, a rate of 0.015 means 15 defective units per 1,000 units sold.

**Historical record:** ClearSweep has defect rate 0.015 proportion. Record status: historical. This figure was reported in the September 2025 monthly report and has since been superseded by the current monitoring cycle. Historical figures are retained in the archived monthly reports and are not to be used for current purchasing decisions.

**1.12.4 Review and Action**

The QA Unit lead reviews the monthly defect rate report within five business days of issue. If a brand partner's defect rate exceeds 0.020 for two consecutive months, the QA Unit lead initiates a supplier review. The supplier review includes:

1. A request for the brand partner's internal quality data
2. A review of returned units, if available
3. A discussion with the brand partner's quality contact
4. A written action plan from the brand partner

The action plan must be received within 20 business days of the review meeting. If the action plan is not received, the matter is escalated to the Contracts Manager.

**1.12.5 Defect Rate Codes**

Each consumer-reported defect is assigned a defect code at the time of data entry. The defect codes are listed below.

| Code | Category | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| D01 | Physical damage | Product arrived damaged, cracked, or broken |
| D02 | Missing parts | Components missing from the package |
| D03 | Functional failure | Product does not work as intended |
| D04 | Cosmetic flaw | Visible imperfection that does not affect function |
| D05 | Incorrect item | Wrong product or variant received |
| D06 | Other | Any defect not fitting the above |

A single defect report may be assigned up to two codes. If more than two codes apply, assign the two most prominent. Record the codes in the defect code field of the SMS record. All coding must be reviewed by a second coder. Disagreements are resolved by the QA Unit lead.

**1.12.6 Spot-Checking Protocol**

Spot-checking is conducted to verify the accuracy of defect rate monitoring. The QA Unit lead selects a random sample of 10 defect reports from the previous month. The selected reports are checked against the original consumer records. The spot-check verifies:
1.12.7 Recording Spot-Check Results

The QA Unit lead records the outcome of each spot-check in the Spot-Check Log (Form QC-14). The log captures the date of the check, the reporting period being verified, the number of reports reviewed, and the number of discrepancies found. A discrepancy is any instance where the coded defect code, the recorded defect category, or the consumer details in the SMS record do not match the original record.

If a discrepancy is found, the QA Unit lead:

1. Corrects the SMS record immediately.
2. Notes the correction in the Correction column of the Spot-Check Log.
3. Advises the data entry officer who created the original record, so that the officer can review their entry practices.

At the end of each quarter, the QA Unit lead summarises the spot-check results. The summary includes the total number of reports checked and the percentage of records containing at least one discrepancy. This summary is included in the quarterly Quality Assurance Report.

1.12.8 Handling of Discrepant Records

Where a spot-check reveals a discrepancy, the SMS record is updated to reflect the correct information. The original entry is not deleted. Instead, the record retains a correction history, showing the original entry, the date of correction, and the name of the QA Unit lead who authorised the change. This correction history is part of the SMS record and is visible to authorised users.

If the discrepancy involves a defect code, the recoded code is entered in the defect code field. The previous code is retained in the correction history. The QA Unit lead initials the change in the audit trail.

1.12.9 Escalation of Systemic Coding Issues

If the quarterly spot-check summary shows that more than 5% of records contain a coding discrepancy, the QA Unit lead escalates the matter to the Quality Manager. The escalation is made in writing, using the Internal Escalation Form (Form QC-17). The form includes:

1. The quarterly summary figures
2. A breakdown of discrepancies by defect code
3. The names of the data entry officers involved
4. A recommended corrective action

The Quality Manager reviews the escalation within ten business days. The Quality Manager may direct additional training for data entry staff, a revision of the coding guidelines, or a full audit of the previous month's defect reports.

1.13 Consumer Complaint Handling

1.13.1 Purpose

This section describes the procedure for handling consumer complaints that are received directly by ACI, rather than through the brand partner's own channels. The procedure ensures that complaints are acknowledged promptly, investigated where necessary, and resolved in a consistent manner.

1.13.2 Receiving a Complaint

Consumer complaints may be received by telephone, email, or through the online contact form. All complaints are logged in the Consumer Complaint Register (Form QC-20) on the day they are received. The register captures the following details:

- Date of receipt
- Consumer name (if provided)
- Contact details (if provided)
- Product name and batch number (if known)
- Description of the issue
- Preferred resolution (if stated by the consumer)

If a complaint is received by telephone, the staff member taking the call completes the register entry while the consumer is on the line. If any detail is not available, the field is left blank and marked with "TBC" (to be confirmed).

1.13.3 Acknowledging a Complaint

Every complaint is acknowledged in writing within two business days of receipt. The acknowledgement is sent by email, or by post if the consumer has no email address. The acknowledgement includes:

1. The complaint reference number
2. A summary of the issue as understood
3. An outline of the next steps
4. The name and contact details of the staff member handling the complaint

The complaint reference number is generated automatically by the register. The format is CC-YYYY-NNN, where YYYY is the year and NNN is a sequential number.

**FINAL RECONCILIATION LOG — ACI**

**Entry 1**  
**Date:** 1 October 2025  
**Prepared by:** M. Tran  
**Reviewed by:** (pending — see note at end of entry)

**1.1 Purpose of this log.** This log records the final reconciliation of discrepancies identified during the September 2025 quality audit cycle. Entries are numbered sequentially and cross-referenced to the source discrepancy reports (DR-2025-xxxx). Where an entry resolves a discrepancy, the resolution is binding for all downstream systems unless a later entry in this log explicitly supersedes it. Any later entry that changes a resolved item must state the earlier entry number and the reason for the change.

**1.2 Discrepancy DR-2025-0914 — ClearSweep version control record.**  
During the audit of the ClearSweep consumer product quality file, the version control register showed two active version numbers for the same product specification. The register entry dated 12 September 2025 listed version 3.0 as current. A separate handwritten note attached to the physical file listed version 3.1 as "current pending review". The discrepancy was logged on 15 September 2025.

**Resolution:** ClearSweep has superseded version 3.1 version. Record status: superseded. The version control register is corrected to show version 3.1 as the superseded version, effective from the date of this entry. The handwritten note is void and has been removed from the physical file. All downstream systems (including the consumer-facing specification database and the internal labelling checklist) must be updated to remove version 3.1 from any "current" status field. The superseded version remains available for historical reference but must not be used for any new compliance assessment.

**Cross-reference:** DR-2025-0914. Related entries: Entry 1.4 below (labelling checklist update), Entry 1.6 (training note for staff handling version control).

**1.3 Procedural note — logging discrepancies.** All staff are reminded that discrepancies must be logged in the central register within two business days of identification. The log entry must include: (a) the discrepancy reference number from the source report, (b) the product or process identifier, (c) a short description of the conflict, and (d) the name of the person who identified the issue. Do not wait for the monthly audit meeting to log a discrepancy. Late logging creates a gap in the reconciliation trail and has been flagged by the external auditor in the past two cycles.

**1.4 Labelling checklist update — ClearSweep.** The labelling checklist (form LC-07, revision B) currently references version 3.1 in section 2, "Specification reference". This entry directs the checklist owner to amend section 2 to show version 3.1 as superseded, with the effective current version to be confirmed by the product manager. The amendment must be made no later than 8 October 2025. The checklist owner is K. Patel. Confirmation of the amendment is to be sent to the ACI mailbox with the subject line "LC-07 revision B — version reference update".

**1.5 Sign-off reminder — all staff.** Entries in this log are not complete until the "Reviewed by" field is filled. The reviewer must be a person other than the preparer and must hold at least Level 2 clearance. Reviewers are expected to check the cross-references and confirm that the resolution does not contradict an earlier entry. If a contradiction is found, the reviewer must raise it in a new entry rather than editing the existing entry. Editing a completed entry is not permitted without a formal change request.

**1.6 Training note — version control handling.** The September audit found that two staff members were unclear on the difference between "superseded" and "withdrawn" in the version control system. For the purpose of this log and the associated quality file: a superseded version is one that has been replaced by a newer version but remains valid for historical reference and may be used for traceability. A withdrawn version is one that has been removed due to an error and must not be relied upon for any purpose. The ClearSweep version 3.1 is classified as superseded, not withdrawn. A short refresher session will be held on 10 October 2025 (meeting room B, 10:00). Attendance is mandatory for staff who handle version control registers.

The label proof dated 29 September 2025 carried the batch prefix "CS-25" in the footer. The production order for that run used "CS-25" in the header but "CS-24" in the packing instruction. Action: ACI mailbox advised 3 October 2025. Confirmation of receipt logged in the quality file.

**1.8 Discrepancy – moisture specification on ClearSweep certificate of analysis (entry ref. 1.1).**

The certificate of analysis for batch CS-25-118 listed moisture as "≤ 5.0%". The approved specification for that product states "≤ 4.5%". The certificate was issued against a superseded specification revision. The current specification revision (SP-09, revision D) governs. A corrected certificate was issued on 6 October 2025 with the value "≤ 4.5%" and a note referencing the specification revision. The superseded certificate has been marked "not for release" in the electronic record.

Reviewer note (J. Okafor, 7 October 2025): Cross-reference to entry 1.4 confirmed. The labelling checklist amendment is dependent on the same specification revision. No contradiction found.

**1.9 Discrepancy – pallet count on despatch docket 20451.**

The despatch docket for order 88231 recorded 24 pallets. The warehouse tally sheet recorded 23 pallets. The delivery driver's signed copy recorded 24 pallets. The warehouse tally sheet was found to be missing the last page. The driver's copy is taken as correct. The tally sheet has been annotated to reflect the missing page and the count reconciled to 24. The discrepancy was resolved at source and no customer notification was required.

Action: Warehouse supervisor to remind loading staff to number all pages of the tally sheet. Reminder issued 6 October 2025.

**1.10 Version control compliance reminder – all staff.**

Following the training note in entry 1.6, a reminder is placed here for staff who handle version control registers. The current version of the document control procedure (PROC-02, revision E) requires that any document that has been replaced be marked "superseded" in the register within two working days of the new version being approved. The register must show the date of supersession and the revision number of the replacement document. Registers that are found to be out of date during the October internal audit will be reported to the quality manager.

The September audit identified two registers that had not been updated for more than a week. Both have since been corrected. Staff are reminded that the register is the primary record for determining which version of a document is current. If a register entry is unclear, the document owner must be asked before the document is used.

**1.11 Unresolved item – supplier corrective action request 2025-14 (ClearSweep label adhesive).**

The corrective action request issued to the label supplier on 12 September 2025 remains open. The supplier has provided a containment action (re-inspection of incoming label rolls) but the root cause analysis has not been received. The due date was 26 September 2025. A follow-up email was sent on 2 October 2025. The supplier has indicated a response by 10 October 2025. This item will be reviewed at the monthly audit meeting on 14 October 2025. If no response is received, the matter will be escalated to the procurement manager.

**1.12 Unresolved item – calibration of pH meter QA-07.**

1. All surveys must be administered in accordance with the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and the Australian Privacy Principles. Participants must be provided with a Privacy Collection Notice (Form ACI-07) prior to commencing any survey.
2. Participants must be at least 18 years of age unless prior written approval has been obtained from the ACI Ethics Committee for a specific project.
3. Surveys are to be conducted in a neutral, non-leading manner. Facilitators must not offer opinions on product quality, pricing, or brand performance before or during a session.
4. Each completed survey must be checked for completeness at the time of collection. If a participant has skipped a question, the facilitator may ask if they wish to answer it, but must not pressure the participant to do so.
5. All paper surveys must be stored in a locked cabinet at the end of each day. Digital survey data must be uploaded to the ACI secure server within 24 hours of session completion.
6. Breaches of these guidelines, whether intentional or accidental, must be reported to the Quality Manager immediately. Do not attempt to correct a breach without authorisation.

**1.4 Participant Recruitment Reminders**

The following reminders are issued to all facilitators. They are not exhaustive but highlight common issues identified during recent audits.

- **Reminder 1 (Issued 14 July 2025):** Recruitment must not be conducted within 10 meters of any retail outlet that sells the ClearSweep product range. This is to avoid capturing an over-representation of recent purchasers. If you are unsure of the distance, err on the side of caution and move further away.
- **Reminder 2 (Issued 28 July 2025):** When approaching potential participants, use the approved script (Appendix B of this Section). Do not improvise or add personal commentary about the product. The script has been designed to minimise bias.
- **Reminder 3 (Issued 11 August 2025):** Do not offer incentives that have not been pre-approved. The only approved incentive for the current round is a $5 coffee voucher, redeemable at participating outlets. Do not offer cash, product samples, or entry into prize draws without checking with the Project Lead first.
- **Reminder 4 (Issued 25 August 2025):** Please ensure you record the recruitment location code accurately on the Session Log (Form ACI-03). Several recent logs have had missing or incorrect codes, which makes data validation difficult. Codes are listed on the inside cover of each facilitator kit.

**1.5 Checklist for Session Setup**

ClearSweep has survey count 240 responses. Record status: historical.

This checklist must be completed for each survey session, prior to the arrival of the first participant. A signed copy of the checklist must be attached to the Session Log at the end of the day.

**Session Setup Checklist (Form ACI-09)**

| Item | Description | Status (OK / N/A) | Initials |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | Station is clean, tidy, and free of distractions. | | |
| 2 | Two chairs available (one for facilitator, one for participant). | | |
| 3 | Table surface is clear of all non-survey materials. | | |
| 4 | Adequate lighting is available. | | |
| 5 | Privacy screen is erected if station is in a public area. | | |
| 6 | Supply of pens (blue or black ink only) is sufficient. | | |
| 7 | Clipboard(s) are in good condition. | | |

**1.6 Session Timing and Scheduling**

- Sessions are typically scheduled in 2-hour blocks. The first 15 minutes of each block are reserved for setup and the final 15 minutes for pack-up and data checks.
- A maximum of 12 participants may be scheduled per 2-hour block. This limit is in place to ensure adequate time for each participant and to maintain data quality.
- If a session is running over time, the facilitator must not rush participants. Instead, note the overrun on the Session Log and adjust the schedule for subsequent sessions, if possible.
- Facilitators should aim for a 5-minute break between participants to allow for data checking and to reset the station.

- If a response is blank, enter `NR` in the database field.
- If a response is ambiguous, flag the form with a sticky note and enter `AMB` in the database field. The form must be reviewed by the Session Coordinator before the end of the week. The Session Coordinator will make a determination and update the database field accordingly.
- If a participant has written a comment in the margins of the survey form, transcribe the comment verbatim into the *Comments* field in the database. Do not edit the comment for spelling or grammar.
- If a participant has circled a response and also written a different response next to it, record the circled response. Note the written response in the *Comments* field.
- If a participant has left a whole page blank, enter `NR` for each question on that page and flag the form for review.

**1.7.2 Data Entry Codes**

The following codes are used in the QC database to standardise data entry. These codes must be used exactly as listed. Do not use free text in coded fields.

| Code | Meaning | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `NR` | No Response | Use when a question is left blank. |
| `AMB` | Ambiguous Response | Use when a response is unclear. Must be reviewed by Session Coordinator. |
| `DK` | Don't Know | Use only if the participant has written "don't know" or similar on the form. |
| `RF` | Refused | Use only if the participant has written "refused" or similar on the form. |
| `OTH` | Other | Use when a response does not fit the provided options, and the participant has written a unique answer. |
| `SP` | Spoiled Form | Use when the form is damaged, illegible, or has been voided. Attach a note to the form. |
| `NA` | Not Applicable | Use only for questions that are conditionally skipped based on a prior response. |

**1.7.3 Data Entry Validation**

After data entry is complete for a session, the facilitator must run the *Session Validation* report. This report lists all records entered for the session, including any `NR`, `AMB`, or `DK` codes. The facilitator must review this report against the physical survey forms.

- Check that the number of records in the report matches the number of forms collected.
- Check that the Participant IDs match the IDs on the forms.
- Check that any `AMB` codes have been resolved or are pending review.
- Sign and date the report, and attach it to the Session Log.

ClearSweep has satisfaction score 4.2 out of 5. Record status: historical.

The Session Coordinator will perform a random audit of at least 10% of entered sessions each week. The audit will compare a sample of database records against the original survey forms. Any discrepancies found during the audit must be corrected immediately, and the correction logged in the *Change Log* (see Section 1.10).

**1.8 Coded Observations**

In addition to survey responses, facilitators may be required to record coded observations during a session. These observations are used to capture non-verbal cues or environmental factors that may affect data quality.

| Code | Meaning | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `O01` | Participant appeared distracted | Note the likely source of distraction. |
| `O02` | Participant asked for clarification on a question | Note the question number. |
| `O03` | Participant took longer than 20 minutes to complete the survey | Note the actual time taken. |
| `O04` | Interruption occurred during the session | Note the nature and duration of the interruption. |
| `O05` | Participant completed the survey without any issues | Standard code for a normal session. |
| `O06` | Equipment failure occurred | Note the equipment and the impact. |

Observations are recorded on the Session Log (Form ACI-03) in the *Observations* column. They are not entered into the QC database unless the Session Coordinator requests it. If an observation is recorded, the facilitator must provide a brief note in the *Comments* column of the Session Log.

**1.9 Survey Instrument Handling**

- All survey forms are numbered sequentially. The form number is printed in the top right corner.
- Forms must be stored in a secure, locked cabinet when not in use.
- Do not photocopy survey forms without the approval of the Session Coordinator.
- If a form is spoiled or voided, mark the form with a diagonal line in red pen and write *VOID* across the front. Do not destroy the form. Attach a note explaining the reason for voiding.
- Completed forms must be transported to the data entry office in a sealed envelope. The envelope must be signed and dated by the facilitator.

**1.11 Spot-Checking Protocol**

Spot-checks are performed to verify that data entry matches the original survey forms. The purpose of a spot-check is to identify systematic errors in data entry, not to re-enter every record.

1.  **Selection of Forms** – The Session Coordinator will select a random sample of completed survey forms for each batch of data entry. The sample size is 15% of the forms in the batch, rounded up to the nearest whole number. If a batch contains fewer than 10 forms, all forms in the batch are spot-checked.
2.  **Comparison** – The spot-checker compares the data entered in the QC database against the original survey form. The comparison must cover all fields on the form, including the form number, all question responses, and any coded observations recorded on the Session Log.
3.  **Recording Results** – The spot-checker records the outcome on the Spot-Check Form (Form ACI-07). For each form checked, the spot-checker writes *PASS* or *FAIL* in the *Outcome* column. If a form fails, the spot-checker must list each discrepancy in the *Discrepancies* column.
4.  **Discrepancy Handling** – If a discrepancy is found, the spot-checker corrects the database record immediately. The correction must be logged in the Change Log (see Section 1.10) with a reference to the spot-check that identified it. The original survey form is not altered.
5.  **Failure Rate** – If more than 5% of the forms in a spot-check sample fail, the entire batch of data entry must be re-checked. The Session Coordinator must be notified, and the data entry operator may be required to repeat a training module.
6.  **Documentation** – Completed Spot-Check Forms are filed with the batch records. They are kept for a minimum of 12 months.

## ACI Quality Control Manual v3.1 — Section 1 (continued)

### 7.3 Spot-Check Protocol — Revised Sampling Rate (effective 05/09/2025)

Following the revised procedure issued 05/09/2025, the sampling rate for spot-checks of completed forms is increased from 10% to 15% per batch. This applies to all batches released on or after that date. For batches already in progress at the time of the revision, the team lead may complete the remaining checks using the 10% rate provided the batch was opened before 05/09/2025. Any check performed after 05/09/2025 on a batch opened earlier should be recorded using the new 15% rate to avoid confusion in the monthly summary.

The table below shows the minimum number of forms to be checked per batch size under both rates for reference:

| Batch size (forms) | 10% rate (min.) | 15% rate (min.) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1–10 | 1 | 2 |
| 11–20 | 2 | 3 |
| 21–30 | 3 | 5 |
| 31–40 | 4 | 6 |
| 41–50 | 5 | 8 |
| 51–60 | 6 | 9 |
| 61–70 | 7 | 11 |
| 71–80 | 8 | 12 |
| 81–90 | 9 | 14 |
| 91–100 | 10 | 15 |

Rounding: always round up to the nearest whole number. Do not round down. If a batch contains 22 forms, the minimum under the 15% rate is 4 (3.3 rounded up), not 3.

---

### 7.4 Handling Discrepancies Found During Spot-Checks

When a spot-check reveals a discrepancy between the form and the database entry, the following steps apply:

1. **Record the discrepancy** on the Spot-Check Form (Form ACI-07) in the Discrepancies column. Include the question number, the value entered in the database, and the value shown on the form. Example: "Q3 response entered as 2, form shows 4".
2. **Notify the data entry operator** responsible for the batch within one working day. Use the internal email address listed in Section 9 (Contacts).
3. **Correct the database entry** to match the paper form, unless the form itself is illegible or incomplete. If the form is the source of the error, escalate to the team lead.
4. **Log the correction** in the Correction Log (Form ACI-09) with the date, operator name, and reason for the change.
5. **Re-check the corrected entry** within 5 working days. The re-check is documented on the same Spot-Check Form row, with the word "RE-CHECKED" added in the Discrepancies column.

If the same operator has three or more discrepancies in a single calendar month, the team lead will arrange a refresher session on data entry procedures. This is not a formal disciplinary step but is intended to reduce repeat errors.

---

### 7.5 Common Data Entry Errors Observed (2025)

The following errors have been observed in recent spot-checks. They are listed here for awareness and to assist operators in self-checking before submission:

- **Transposed digits** — e.g., entering 1086 instead of 1085 for the form number. This usually happens when the operator reads the form quickly. Always read the number twice.
- **Scale confusion** — entering a response on a 5-point scale as 3 when the form shows 2. This occurs more often with questions that use a 1–5 scale than with yes/no questions.
- **Blank responses** — leaving a question blank in the database when the form has a valid response. This is often due to skipping a field during data entry. Use the "tab" key to move through fields systematically rather than clicking.
- **Duplicate entries** — the same form number entered twice. This is rare but has occurred when a batch is split across two operators. Check the batch register before starting.

Operators are reminded that the form is the source of truth. If there is any doubt about a response, do not guess — leave the field blank and flag the form for review by the team lead.

---

### 7.6 Spot-Check Results Summary — August 2025

The following summary covers spot-checks conducted in August 2025, using the 10% sampling rate in effect at that time. The revised 15% rate applies from September 2025 onward.

**1.6 Handling Survey Responses**

All responses are recorded in the central survey system under the session ID. The following rules apply:

- Each response is counted individually, even if the participant did not answer every question.
- Responses are considered final once the participant submits the survey. Do not alter responses after submission.
- If a response is incomplete, mark it as partial in the system. Do not discard partial responses.

**1.8 Common Errors and Corrections**

**1.10.3 Handling Missing Responses**

A missing response occurs when a participant has not answered a question. Missing responses are distinct from "N/A" responses and must be coded as such.

The code 99 must not be used for any other purpose. If a response record contains more than two missing responses for a single participant, flag the record in the Data Entry Log and notify the QA Unit lead. The record may still be entered, but the flag must be recorded.

**1.10.4 Coding Conventions for Open Comments**

Open comments are coded for theme analysis. Coding is performed after data entry is complete and verified. The following convention codes are current for the survey cycle commencing September 2025:

| Code | Theme | Example Phrasing |

A single comment may be assigned up to two codes. If a comment relates to more than two themes, assign the two most prominent. Record the codes in the coding field of the SMS record. All coding must be reviewed by a second coder. Disagreements are resolved by the QA Unit lead.

**1.10.5 Verification**

After data entry for a batch is complete, the Verifier must check the entered data against the original response records. The Verifier checks:

1. All numeric responses match the original record.
2. All open comments are transcribed verbatim.
3. All missing responses are coded 99.
4. All brand partner codes match the drop-down list.

The Verifier records the outcome on the Data Entry Log. If discrepancies are found, the Verifier returns the batch to the Data Entry Officer for correction. Once corrected, the batch is re-verified. A batch may be returned a maximum of two times. After the second return, the batch is referred to the QA Unit lead.

**1.10.6 Batch Completion and Upload**

Once verified, the batch is uploaded to the SMS. Upload must occur on the same day as verification. After upload, print the batch summary report from the SMS and attach it to the Data Entry Log. File the completed log in the QA filing cabinet within two business days.

Each survey session generates a session record. The session record includes:

Session records are retained for a minimum of 24 months from the session date. After 24 months, records are moved to the archived storage area in the basement. Archived records are kept for a further 36 months before destruction. Destruction must be recorded on the Destruction Log, including the date, the record range, and the name of the staff member who performed the destruction.

If a record is subject to a current complaint, dispute, or regulatory review, it is placed on hold. Held records are not destroyed until the hold is lifted in writing by the QA Unit lead. The hold status is noted in red on the folder cover.

**1.12 Defect Rate Monitoring**

Defect rate monitoring is a monthly activity. The purpose is to track the proportion of defective units reported by consumers across all brand partners. The monitoring process is described below.

**1.12.1 Scope**

Monitoring covers all brand partners who have a current supply agreement with ACI. For each brand partner, the monthly defect rate is calculated from consumer-reported defects in the SMS. The calculation uses the number of defective units reported divided by the total units sold for that month.

**1.12.2 Data Source**

The SMS is the only data source for defect rate monitoring. Manual counts or estimates from other systems are not to be used. If the SMS is unavailable, the monthly monitoring report is deferred until the SMS is restored. Deferred reports are noted as "deferred" on the monthly summary.

**1.12.3 Reporting Format**

The monthly defect rate report follows the template in Appendix C. The report lists each brand partner, the total units sold, the number of defective units reported, and the calculated defect rate. Rates are expressed as a proportion to three decimal places. For example, a rate of 0.015 means 15 defective units per 1,000 units sold.

**Historical record:** ClearSweep has defect rate 0.015 proportion. Record status: historical. This figure was reported in the September 2025 monthly report and has since been superseded by the current monitoring cycle. Historical figures are retained in the archived monthly reports and are not to be used for current purchasing decisions.

**1.12.4 Review and Action**

The QA Unit lead reviews the monthly defect rate report within five business days of issue. If a brand partner's defect rate exceeds 0.020 for two consecutive months, the QA Unit lead initiates a supplier review. The supplier review includes:

1. A request for the brand partner's internal quality data
2. A review of returned units, if available
3. A discussion with the brand partner's quality contact
4. A written action plan from the brand partner

The action plan must be received within 20 business days of the review meeting. If the action plan is not received, the matter is escalated to the Contracts Manager.

**1.12.5 Defect Rate Codes**

Each consumer-reported defect is assigned a defect code at the time of data entry. The defect codes are listed below.

| Code | Category | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| D01 | Physical damage | Product arrived damaged, cracked, or broken |
| D02 | Missing parts | Components missing from the package |
| D03 | Functional failure | Product does not work as intended |
| D04 | Cosmetic flaw | Visible imperfection that does not affect function |
| D05 | Incorrect item | Wrong product or variant received |
| D06 | Other | Any defect not fitting the above |

A single defect report may be assigned up to two codes. If more than two codes apply, assign the two most prominent. Record the codes in the defect code field of the SMS record. All coding must be reviewed by a second coder. Disagreements are resolved by the QA Unit lead.

**1.12.6 Spot-Checking Protocol**

1.12.7 Recording Spot-Check Results

The QA Unit lead records the outcome of each spot-check in the Spot-Check Log (Form QC-14). The log captures the date of the check, the reporting period being verified, the number of reports reviewed, and the number of discrepancies found. A discrepancy is any instance where the coded defect code, the recorded defect category, or the consumer details in the SMS record do not match the original record.

If a discrepancy is found, the QA Unit lead:

1. Corrects the SMS record immediately.
2. Notes the correction in the Correction column of the Spot-Check Log.
3. Advises the data entry officer who created the original record, so that the officer can review their entry practices.

At the end of each quarter, the QA Unit lead summarises the spot-check results. The summary includes the total number of reports checked and the percentage of records containing at least one discrepancy. This summary is included in the quarterly Quality Assurance Report.

1.12.8 Handling of Discrepant Records

Where a spot-check reveals a discrepancy, the SMS record is updated to reflect the correct information. The original entry is not deleted. Instead, the record retains a correction history, showing the original entry, the date of correction, and the name of the QA Unit lead who authorised the change. This correction history is part of the SMS record and is visible to authorised users.

If the discrepancy involves a defect code, the recoded code is entered in the defect code field. The previous code is retained in the correction history. The QA Unit lead initials the change in the audit trail.

1.12.9 Escalation of Systemic Coding Issues

If the quarterly spot-check summary shows that more than 5% of records contain a coding discrepancy, the QA Unit lead escalates the matter to the Quality Manager. The escalation is made in writing, using the Internal Escalation Form (Form QC-17). The form includes:

1. The quarterly summary figures
2. A breakdown of discrepancies by defect code
3. The names of the data entry officers involved
4. A recommended corrective action

The Quality Manager reviews the escalation within ten business days. The Quality Manager may direct additional training for data entry staff, a revision of the coding guidelines, or a full audit of the previous month's defect reports.

1.13 Consumer Complaint Handling

1.13.1 Purpose

This section describes the procedure for handling consumer complaints that are received directly by ACI, rather than through the brand partner's own channels. The procedure ensures that complaints are acknowledged promptly, investigated where necessary, and resolved in a consistent manner.

1.13.2 Receiving a Complaint

Consumer complaints may be received by telephone, email, or through the online contact form. All complaints are logged in the Consumer Complaint Register (Form QC-20) on the day they are received. The register captures the following details:

- Date of receipt
- Consumer name (if provided)
- Contact details (if provided)
- Product name and batch number (if known)
- Description of the issue
- Preferred resolution (if stated by the consumer)

If a complaint is received by telephone, the staff member taking the call completes the register entry while the consumer is on the line. If any detail is not available, the field is left blank and marked with "TBC" (to be confirmed).

1.13.3 Acknowledging a Complaint

Every complaint is acknowledged in writing within two business days of receipt. The acknowledgement is sent by email, or by post if the consumer has no email address. The acknowledgement includes:

1. The complaint reference number
2. A summary of the issue as understood
3. An outline of the next steps
4. The name and contact details of the staff member handling the complaint

The complaint reference number is generated automatically by the register. The format is CC-YYYY-NNN, where YYYY is the year and NNN is a sequential number.
